rationale: M49.G1 wave (family parity with java's overload-arity-varargs-multicatch): (1) multi-catch `catch (IOException | SQLException e)` emits a declared_type References edge for EACH union member — the pre-fix walk had no catch_formal_parameter case at all so both types silently vanished from the type-usage graph; the `e` parameter is not a type and must never appear as a target. (2) Varargs `int... xs` overriding array `int[] xs` resolves exact-in-file (JLS 8.4.1 same-signature family contract).

expectRelationships.note: CHANNEL pin for the multi-catch collector, on the QUALIFIED union the analyzer can actually report. The rows above name the bare IOException / SQLException / Exception and are unmet today, because the collector emits a declared_type reference only for a name containing a `.` - so no row in the lane observed the catch_formal_parameter case, and deleting that case outright changed no verdict. `declaredOn` is the load-bearing part: it is what distinguishes a catch union member from the same name appearing in a throws clause or a local. `from` is left unconstrained so the enclosing-type attribution stays a separate question.
the SECOND union member: JLS 14.20 parity is a per-member contract, so one row per member keeps a regression that emits only the first type visible
